'''Christof Wetterich''' (born 12 April 1952) is a German [[theoretical physicist]]. He is a professor of theoretical physics at the [[Heidelberg University]]. He is known for his work on the [[seesaw mechanism|Seesaw mechanism in grand unification theory (GUT)]], [[Quintessence (physics)|quintessence]], the [[Wetterich equation]] for the [[functional renormalization group]] (FRG) and [[asymptotic safety in quantum gravity]].

==Early life and education ==
Wetterich was born in [[Freiburg]] on 12 April 1952. He studied physics at the [[University of Paris VII]], the [[University of Cologne]] and the [[Freiburg University]], where he received his Ph.D. in 1979 and was [[habilitation|habilitated]] in 1983.

== Research and career ==
His primary research interests are [[cosmology]] and [[quantum field theory]]. Two of his notable theoretical developments are [[Quintessence (physics)|quintessence]] and the [[functional renormalization group]]. These methods have found applications in many areas of physics. Functional renormalization provides a suitable framework for studying [[quantum gravity]] ([[Asymptotic safety in quantum gravity|asymptotic safety]]),<ref>{{cite journal | last=Reuter | first=M. | title=Nonperturbative evolution equation for quantum gravity | journal=Physical Review D | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=57 | issue=2 | date=1998-01-15 | issn=0556-2821 | doi=10.1103/physrevd.57.971 | pages=971–985|arxiv=hep-th/9605030v1| bibcode=1998PhRvD..57..971R }}</ref> [[Yang–Mills theory|Yang–Mills theories]]<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Reuter | first1=M. | last2=Wetterich | first2=C. | title=Effective average action for gauge theories and exact evolution equations | journal=Nuclear Physics B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=417 | issue=1–2 | year=1994 | issn=0550-3213 | doi=10.1016/0550-3213(94)90543-6 | pages=181–214| bibcode=1994NuPhB.417..181R | url=https://bib-pubdb1.desy.de/search?p=id:%22PUBDB-2023-00426%22 }}</ref> and it was also useful in non-relativistic quantum systems such as [[BCS theory|BCS]] to [[Bose–Einstein condensate|BEC]] crossover where it ''bridges'' the two theories in a unified theoretical language.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Diehl | first1=S. | last2=Gies | first2=H. | last3=Pawlowski | first3=J. M. | last4=Wetterich | first4=C. | title=Flow equations for the BCS-BEC crossover | journal=Physical Review A | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=76 | issue=2 | date=2007-08-01 | issn=1050-2947 | doi=10.1103/physreva.76.021602 | article-number=021602|arxiv=cond-mat/0701198| bibcode=2007PhRvA..76b1602D }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Diehl | first1=S. | last2=Floerchinger | first2=S. | last3=Gies | first3=H. | last4=Pawlowkski | first4=J.M. | last5=Wetterich | first5=C. | title=Functional renormalization group approach to the BCS-BEC crossover | journal=Annalen der Physik | publisher=Wiley | date=2010-07-19 | issn=0003-3804 | doi=10.1002/andp.201010458 | volume=552|issue=9|pages=615–656|arxiv=0907.2193| bibcode=2010AnP...522..615D }}</ref>

In 1977–1986, he performed fundamental calculations for the theoretical understanding of tiny neutrino masses in GUT.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Lazarides | first1=G. | last2=Shafi | first2=Q. | last3=Wetterich | first3=C. | title=Proton lifetime and fermion masses in an SO(10) model | journal=Nuclear Physics B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=181 | issue=2 | year=1981 | issn=0550-3213 | doi=10.1016/0550-3213(81)90354-0 | pages=287–300| bibcode=1981NuPhB.181..287L }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Magg |first=M. |last2=Wetterich |first2=Ch. |date=1980-07-14 |title=Neutrino mass problem and gauge hierarchy |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0370269380908254 |journal=Physics Letters B |volume=94 |issue=1 |pages=61–64 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(80)90825-4 |issn=0370-2693|url-access=subscription }}</ref>  This work was incorporated into the [[seesaw mechanism|Type II seesaw mechanism]] in subsequent studies.

In 1987–2001, he completed two of his two best known theoretical proposals: the dynamical [[Dark Energy|dark energy]] or quintessence model, developed in 1987.,<ref>{{cite journal | last=Wetterich | first=C. | title=Cosmology and the fate of dilatation symmetry | journal=Nuclear Physics B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=302 | issue=4 | year=1988 | issn=0550-3213 | doi=10.1016/0550-3213(88)90193-9 | pages=668–696| arxiv=1711.03844 | bibcode=1988NuPhB.302..668W }}</ref><ref>''The Cosmon Model for an Asymptotically Vanishing Time Dependent Cosmological "Constant"'', C. Wetterich, Astron. Astrophys. '''301''', 321 (1995), [https://arxiv.org/abs/arXiv:hep-th/9408025 arXiv:hep-th/9408025v1]</ref> which could explain the observed accelerated expansion of the universe. The functional renormalization group relates macroscopic physical structures to microscopic physical laws through to a renormalization group of effective average actions. Its basic formula is the [[Functional renormalization group#The flow equation for the effective action|Wetterich equation]] (or FRG Flow Equation). He developed this in 1993<ref>{{cite journal | last=Wetterich | first=Christof | title=Exact evolution equation for the effective potential | journal=Physics Letters B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=301 | issue=1 | year=1993 | issn=0370-2693 | doi=10.1016/0370-2693(93)90726-x | pages=90–94| arxiv=1710.05815 | bibcode=1993PhLB..301...90W }}</ref> 
and a review of FRG was published in 2001.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Berges | first1=Jürgen | last2=Tetradis | first2=Nikolaos | last3=Wetterich | first3=Christof | title=Non-perturbative renormalization flow in quantum field theory and statistical physics | journal=Physics Reports | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=363 | issue=4–6 | year=2002 | issn=0370-1573 | doi=10.1016/s0370-1573(01)00098-9 | pages=223–386|arxiv=hep-ph/0005122| bibcode=2002PhR...363..223B }}</ref>

In 2013, based on dilatation symmetry, he proposed the cosmon field model, in which the Planck mass increases but there is no big bang singularity.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Wetterich | first=Christof | title=universe without expansion | journal=Physics of the Dark Universe | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=2 | issue=4 | year=2013 | doi=10.1016/j.dark.2013.10.002 | pages=184–187| arxiv=1303.6878 | bibcode=2013PDU.....2..184W }}</ref>

He has worked at [[CERN]] in Geneva and [[DESY]] in Hamburg. Since 1992 he has held a professorship in theoretical physics at the [[Heidelberg University|Ruprecht-Karls-Universität Heidelberg]].

==Honours and awards==
In 2005, Wetterich received the [[Max Planck Society|Max-Planck]] Research Prize.<ref>There exists a short public [http://www.humboldt-foundation.de/movies/MaxPlanckForschungspreis05_low.flv video] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120322032101/http://www.humboldt-foundation.de/movies/MaxPlanckForschungspreis05_low.flv |date=2012-03-22 }} (German) as a film portrait to the winners in addition.</ref> Since 2006 he is member of the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences.<ref>[http://webarchive.loc.gov/all/20120110032036/http%3A//www.adw.uni%2Dheidelberg.de/gs2/mitglieder%2Ddb/haw%2Dmitglieder%2Deintrag.php?quelle%3Dimperia%26id%3D265%26sprache%3Den%26benutzer%3Dadw_gast%26kennwort%3Dg123st Portrait] at the [http://www.haw.uni-heidelberg.de/index.en.html HAW homepage]</ref>
